- When sentiment shows strong positive spikes followed by sharp declines, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next period.
- If sentiment turns negative sharply after a rally, model often fails to adjust quickly — lower forecast by 3–8% in lagged period.
- Model consistently overestimates prices during high-news-volume periods — scale down forecast by 2–5% if news volume > 3.0.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment rises >0.67 and then drops, forecast should be capped at 10% below peak for next 3 days.
- Forecast horizon error: 30-day models often overestimate early in cycle — adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or negative in last 3 days.
- If sentiment change is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day until sentiment stabilizes.
